transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Liang (Redwood CSM); Aisha Rahman (Evercrest Head of MLOps), Tom Keller (Infra), Priya Nair (Security), Ben Ortiz (Product)

--- Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Evercrest is approaching renewal, wants to add APAC region capacity and explore a private/VPC deployment for regulated flows; primary concerns are data residency, key management, and predictable latency. Asked about dedicated reserved capacity vs burst. Redwood to send pricing and run pilot.

00:00 Maya (AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we've got a pretty tight agenda so we'll start with a quick status, then Samir will walk through the technical plan for APAC and VPC peering, and then open for Q&A. does that sound good?
00:07 Aisha (Evercrest): yep that works for us, thanks maya. real quick, timeline — renewal is end of month right? we want to lock in something before holidays.
00:13 Maya: yeah renewal window is 12/31, we can align the new contract to start 1/1; you mentioned wanting a top-up for capacity and an APAC node — what's the target qps and expected token volume?
00:24 Aisha: so baseline is around 600 qps across models right now, peak is closer to 1.6k qps during end-of-day batch jobs. the thing is we expect APAC traffic to grow fast once we open the singapore region — target there is maybe 300 steady qps first quarter, bursting to 800 on promos.
00:40 Tom (Infra): and importantly we need predictable tail latency under 100ms at p95 for customer-facing endpoints. some offline jobs can tolerate higher.
00:48 Samir (SE): okay good, so couple options: reserved Dedicated pool in APAC for steady capacity + burst credits, or hosted APAC with smart routing and fast fallback to US when capacity is saturated. reserved gives predictability for latency but cost is higher; hosted is more flexible but you can see cross-region variance.
01:03 Priya (Security): quick point on data: regulated workflows (payments PII) we want to keep in region or on private network. is private deployment (VPC) required for that, or can we do tenancy isolation?
01:15 Samir: you can do either — Dedicated with VPC peering keeps traffic inside your VPC and we support customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your control. If you need on-prem air-gapped we also have an onprem package but that's heavier.
01:28 Ben (Product): can you run model fallbacks? e.g., if the big model isn't available in APAC, automatically route to a smaller variant without failing the call?
01:36 Samir: yep that's built into the runtime, we call it variant routing; you can set policies by latency or cost. there are also graceful degradation rules so you don't get hard 5xx.
01:45 Tom: any idea about egress/load balancing — we use a strict firewall posture, will we need static IP ranges for outbound?
01:52 Maya: we'll provide the APICID ranges and documented egress IPs; for VPC peering we'll share the BGP routes and firewall rules.
01:58 Aisha: okay good. on compliance, Priya is going to want SOC2 docs and also details about audit logging retention.
02:05 Priya: yes audit logs are critical — retention 7 years ideally, or at least exportability to our SIEM. also need KMS integration details: do you support HSM-backed keys?
02:16 Rosa (CSM): we do support cloud KMS and HSM options depending on the private deployment; i'll attach the integration guide. logs are exportable, we've sent Splunk/Elastic examples to other customers.
02:25 Priya: sometimes the transcripts get redacted automatically — is that configurable? we need token-level redaction for PCI scope reduction.
02:32 Samir: we have prefix/KV caching and a redaction pipeline; we can set filters at ingest to scrub sensitive fields. note though this affects eval fidelity; we'll document tradeoffs.
02:44 Aisha: on pricing, are burst credits billed differently — we saw a big bill spike last quarter and want to avoid surprises.
02:50 Maya: yes burst is billed at a premium per-token rate; reserved capacity amortizes lower. we can structure a blended agreement — baseline reserved + burst for seasonal spikes. i'll include examples in the quote.
03:01 Ben: curious too — do you have latency SLAs for p95 in region with reserved capacity?
03:07 Maya: for Dedicated with pax commits we offer SLA-backed latency targets, we can include p95 numbers in the contract appendix. i'll have legal flex those details.
03:15 Tom: okay tech deep dive, Samir? 
03:17 Samir: sure, i'll share my screen in a sec — (audio: screen share noise) so architecture: for APAC we recommend a small reserved node pool sized to your projected steady qps (say 300 qps), plus a shared burst pool in region. plan is to pre-warm KV caches for the most common prefixes to keep tail latency low. one caveat: large attention cache spills can cause transient p99 spikes if a single request suddenly expands sequence length, we recommend request size limits.
03:46 Aisha: we run long-form summaries too, sequences up to 2.5k tokens sometimes. will that be an issue?
03:52 Samir: the runtime supports long sequences with optimized attention kernels but it does increase cost and can increase variability. we can set routing for long-form jobs to dedicated batch nodes so user requests stay snappy.
04:08 Tom: network question again — VPC peering adds an extra hop, do you see an appreciable delta in latency?
04:14 Samir: peering typically adds sub-ms for cross-AZ in region; most of the latency is model compute not network. the larger factor is cold-start model load. that'll be mitigated with hot warm pools.
04:27 Aisha: about the pilot — we'd like to run an APAC perf pilot with our real traffic for 48 hours, can you support that?
04:33 Maya: yes we can. typical pilot is 24-72 hours; scope: real traffic replay to dedicated APAC node with telemetry. Samir will set up runbook and metrics to capture p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and model fallback rates.
04:44 Samir: i'll prepare a pilot plan with exact metrics and thresholds; we'll request a sample of your traffic profile and a toggle to replay.
04:50 Ben: what about canary deployment for new model versions? we need gradual rollouts with rollback policy.
04:56 Samir: supported — canary percentages per route, automated rollback on quality regressions tied to eval sets; Redwood Optimize can flag quality regressions.
05:07 Priya: security follow-ups: we need an attestation for data residency and a runbook for incident response. also confirm SAML SSO and RBAC mapping.
05:18 Rosa: yes we support SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role mapping. i'll attach SSO doc. incident response runbook and incident SLAs are part of our enterprise pack.
05:27 Aisha: referencing competitors briefly — NimbusWorks pitched lower price but their APAC footprint is smaller; they also didn't have KMS/HSM support out of the box which worried us.
05:38 Maya: good to know. we try to balance unit economics and predictability; our Optimize team can generate a quantization recommendation to reduce cost on non-critical routes.
05:48 Tom: question — can we do per-route quantization so customer support bots use int8 while payment flows stay fp16?
05:55 Samir: yes per-model/per-route quantization profiles are supported; you'll want to register evals to monitor quality drift.
06:03 Ben: timeline — if we sign by 12/31, when can APAC nodes be hot?
06:08 Maya: with reserved provisioning and pre-warm, we can activate within 10 business days for APAC. for VPC-enabled Dedicated it can take 14 business days due to networking and your change windows.
06:18 Aisha: that's fine, we can target provisioning in mid-Jan.
06:22 Priya: about keys — we run a Thales HSM, need to confirm integration. is there an existing connector?
06:28 Samir: we have connectors for the major HSM vendors; for Thales we usually do an HSM broker pattern and keep customer key operations inside your HSM. i'll include a vendor-specific checklist.
06:40 Tom: brakes — we have a dev constraint: our staging uses a stripped-down model set, can we do a staging-to-prod migration plan?
06:46 Samir: yes we support environment promotion; the console lets you pin model versions and rollout policies per environment. we recommend smoke tests in staging then a phased promotion.
06:58 Aisha: great. any blockers from your side?
07:01 Maya: not blockers; next steps are commercial and technical prep. i'll send the blended quote with reserved + burst numbers and a proposed contract term. Samir will send VPC runbook and pilot plan. Rosa will surface SSO and compliance docs.
07:13 Priya: one more thing — audit log retention, can you guarantee immutable logs for 7 years?
07:19 Rosa: we can export logs to your archival S3 with immutability locks; in private deployments we can keep them in-region. we'll note the options.
07:28 Ben: question on billing granularity — do you meter by token and by embedding unit? we use both heavily.
07:34 Maya: yes tokens and embeddings are metered; we'll include the blended unit costs in the sheet. you can also set hard spend caps by route.
07:44 Aisha: okay this was helpful, thanks. let's recap next steps.
07:47 Maya: recap: 1) Maya send pricing and SLA appendix (due 12/04). 2) Samir prepare pilot runbook and VPC checklist (due 12/07). 3) Evercrest to provide traffic profiles and HSM details (Aisha/Priya due 12/06 & 12/08). 4) Schedule pilot for week of 12/14 if timing works.
07:59 Ben: works for product & infra.
08:02 Tom: one tiny nit: can we get a list of APAC region node SKUs? we have cost center mapping.
08:08 Maya: yes i'll include SKU breakdown in the spreadsheet.
08:11 Aisha: awesome. thanks everyone.
08:14 (meeting wraps)
